scenes.name: hook
scenes.text: A share price on your app keeps changing every second. So who is actually setting that price?

scenes.name: exchange
scenes.text: In India, shares trade on exchanges like NSE and BSE. Your broker's app sends your order there.

scenes.name: book
scenes.text: For every stock, the exchange keeps an order book. Buyers list the highest price they'll pay, and sellers list the lowest they'll accept.

scenes.name: match
scenes.text: When a buy price meets a sell price, a computer matches them instantly. That's a trade.

scenes.name: ltp
scenes.text: The price you see is simply the last traded price. Every new trade can nudge it up or down.

scenes.name: news
scenes.text: Good news brings more buyers, who bid higher. Bad news brings more sellers, who ask lower. Supply and demand, every second.

scenes.name: settle
scenes.text: After the trade, the shares and money actually change hands one working day later, called T plus one settlement.

scenes.name: outro
scenes.text: Orders, book, match, price. A crowd setting a number. Follow for more on how things really work.
